harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s invoice exporter. It now uses unique mode-0600 temporary files beside the destination, atomically publishes complete exports, replaces rather than follows destination symlinks, preserves existing destinations on failure, and cleans temporary files. The source and protected sentinel remained unchanged, including after reboot.
actions_performed: Replaced the fixed tmp/export.tmp workflow with legacy-compatible mktemp usage, restrictive umask, cleanup traps, and atomic mv -T publication.
Verified normal export, malicious destination symlink handling, controlled partial-read failure, cleanup, and 12 concurrent exports.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified a changed boot identity, retained CentOS 5.11/kernel 2.6.18-398.el5, persisted utility, intact source/sentinel, and successful post-restart export.

evidence.summary: Confirmed the legacy mktemp interface and installed a syntax-valid root-owned executable.

evidence.requirement: Successful exports retain all invoice rows and symlinks cannot redirect writes
evidence.summary: Normal and symlink-path outputs exactly matched the 3-line source; the sentinel retained checksum 1728658330.

evidence.requirement: Failures preserve the prior destination and remove temporary files
evidence.summary: A forced partial-read failure returned nonzero, left the prior destination checksum unchanged, and left no temporary residue.

evidence.requirement: Concurrent exports use private temporary files
evidence.summary: Observed 12 distinct mode-0600 temporary files during overlapping exports; all completed with exact output and no residue.

evidence.requirement: Preserve source data and protected sentinel
evidence.summary: Pre-change and post-restart checksums remained 321984193 for invoices.csv and 1728658330 for protected.txt.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 34477d20-3c59-40f3-8000-000000000000, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 1c77cc42-8f41-4ea2-8000-000000000000, and direct post-restart utility/data recovery proof.
